title: Faith justifies as disposition (act) or as part of formal cause (habit)
source_text: XLVII. Caeterum fidem justificare dicunt per modum dispositionis, aut etiam tanquam justitiae partem & initium; quo respectu revocatur fides ad causam formalem justificationis. Ad cujus rei intelligentiam, observandum est Doctores Ecclesiae Romanae per justificationem non significare solam a peccatis absolutionem, sed renovationem quoque interioris hominis, quam sanctificationis nomine designamus. Ac praeterea fidem duobus modis ab illis accipi: Et 1. quidem pro actu fidei, qui per actuale Dei auxilium in anima excitatur, priusquam adepta sit gratiam habitualem: 2. Pro fidei habitu, qui cum habitibus spei & charitatis, in jam credentis animam infunditur. Priori modo sumpta fides justificat, ex eorum mente, per modum dispositionis: quia per illam anima praeparatur & disponitur ad accipiendam a Deo remissionem peccatorum, & simul quoque justitiam illam habitualem, a qua justi sanctique fideles in Scriptura vocantur. Fides vero sumpta posteriori modo pertinet ad causam formalem justificationis: quoniam est pars novae illius justitiae, quam Spiritus Sanctus in fidelibus creat, & per quam illos vere & reapse justos, sanctosque constituit.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover they say that faith justifies by way of disposition, or even as a part and beginning of righteousness; in which respect faith is referred to the formal cause of justification. For understanding this, it must be observed that the Doctors of the Roman Church by justification do not signify only absolution from sins, but also the renovation of the interior man, which we designate by the name of sanctification. And further that faith is taken by them in two ways: and (1) indeed for the act of faith, which by God's actual help is stirred in the soul before habitual grace has been obtained; (2) for the habit of faith, which with the habits of hope and charity is infused into the soul of one already believing. Faith taken in the former way justifies, on their view, by way of disposition: because by it the soul is prepared and disposed to receive from God the remission of sins, and at the same time also that habitual righteousness by which the faithful are called just and holy in Scripture. But faith taken in the latter way pertains to the formal cause of justification: since it is a part of that new righteousness which the Holy Spirit creates in the faithful, and by which he constitutes them truly and in reality just and holy.
pass_b_english: Rome: faith-as-act disposes for justification; faith-as-habit is part of infused righteousness.
Their 'justification' includes forgiveness and interior renovation (sanctification).

choices.english: act of faith ... habit of faith
choices.why: Roman double sense of how faith relates to justification.
